AI SEO tools use artificial intelligence and machine learning to automate SEO tasks that traditionally took hours or days to complete manually. Instead of spending 10 hours manually analyzing competitor keywords or checking hundreds of pages for technical issues, AI SEO software handles it in minutes. This frees your team to focus on strategy and execution rather than repetitive analysis. These tools help with keyword research, content optimization, rank tracking , technical audits, and – increasingly – monitoring brand visibility across AI platforms like ChatGPT and Perplexity. Why Do You Need One? SEO complexity is accelerating. Google’s algorithm updates happen constantly, AI Overviews are changing search behavior, and competitors publish faster than ever. AI SEO tools help you keep pace without burning out your team. That said, not all tools deliver equal value. Some provide genuinely useful insights. Others repackage basic data and slap “AI-powered” on the label. The difference comes down to accuracy, speed, and whether the tool actually helps you rank better – or just creates more busywork. I test new platforms for at least 3 months across multiple client accounts. If keyword volumes are consistently off by more than 15-20%, or the tool suggests optimizations that contradict GSC data, I move on. AI Capabilities Look beyond basic automation. The best tools use AI to: – Analyze search intent across top-ranking pages – Predict ranking difficulty for *your specific domain* (not generic scores) – Track visibility in AI-powered search results like ChatGPT and Perplexity – Suggest content improvements based on competitor analysis Workflow Compatibility A great tool fits into your existing process without forcing you to rebuild everything. Can you export data easily? Does it integrate with Google Docs or WordPress? Will your team actually use it, or will it sit unused after the first week? Integrations Check if it connects with Google Search Console, GA4, and your CMS. Tools that play well with your existing setup save hours of manual data transfers. Bonus points if it syncs with project management tools like Asana or Notion. Pricing Be honest about your budget and team size. Some tools charge per user seat, others by the number of projects or keywords tracked. Monthly plans offer flexibility, but annual subscriptions usually save 20 to 30 percent. Always test the free trial before committing. Data Quality The best tools would pull reliable data sources and update frequently. Real-time rank tracking matters more than monthly snapshots. If the tool shows stale data or can’t explain where numbers come from, move on. Scalability Will this tool grow with your business? If you manage 3 sites now but plan to scale to 20, check the pricing tiers and feature limits. Some platforms become prohibitively expensive as you add more domains or users. Today, I reveal them all to you in this mega guide. Post by Omid G | June 14, 2026 I've been doing SEO for a decade. Most notably, I led SEO at Webflow (a $4.2B company) and then built my blog to +150K visitors/month from SEO all by myself. I've also worked with dozens of software companies to help them with their SEO revenue growth. It's safe to say that I've tested and used all of the best SEO tools on the market. And I'm constantly looking for the newest tools that can give me and my clients an edge. In this post, I'm breaking down 24 of the best SEO software and tools (across different categories) so you can pick what's best for your specific needs. I'll also include an "ease of use" score for each tool (beginner, intermediate, or advanced) to help you choose tools that match your skill level. These aren't in a particular order, but they lean a bit more on the side of how much I value them. Also, I tried to group many of the tools for logical clarity so you can easily find what you're looking for. Don't worry, this is not a biased post by some SEO company trying to sell you their tool. This post is 100% written by me. I only recommend the SEO tools I've used, and will talk about what I like and don't like about each of them. No AI-generated slop, just real insights from someone who uses these tools every single day. What is an SEO tool? An SEO (search engine optimization) tool is a platform that helps you plan and strategize ways to improve your site's visibility in search engines. This is not just limited to Google. This includes Bing, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and all the other search engines on the market. These tools all do different things. Some of them help you with keyword research , some of them help are search ranking tools that help you analyze competitors' traffic and backlinks, some of them help you create content that is optimized for search engines, some of them help you create automated SEO workflows, and some of them help you improve the technical health of your website. Some of the tools we'll go over in this post aim to do all the things I just mentioned, while some of them only do one specific thing very well. Overall, I've used every single tool on this list and have written a comprehensive review of all of them below. But my goal is to help you understand what tool to use for yourself, so let's first go over what I consider to be the best SEO tools to use. What do I consider the best SEO tools? For beginners, I generally recommend using the free SEO tools that Google gives you. This includes using Google Autocomplete, Google Keyword Planner, Google Search Console, and even Google Trends. With just these free tools alone, I've been able to rank #1 really fast. In fact, here are my top SEO tools if you prefer to watch how I use them: The Google tools are some of the best free tools (and I'll show you more in this post) that I think you should start out with first. From there, you want to get into the content creation part, and some of the tools that I believe are the best there would be Surfer, Claude, or Clearscope. When it comes to keyword research and analyzing competitors, my favorite tools are Ahrefs, Semrush, and using Google Autocomplete. And when it comes to creating SEO automations, my favorite tool by far is Gumloop. Again, all of these we're going to go over below. Okay, no more rambling. Let's get into my picks for the best SEO software. 24 best SEO tools I've personally tested in 2026 Here are the best SEO tools right now: ‍ Google Search Console (best for first-party data + indexing) ‍ Google Autocomplete (best for search-intent discovery) ‍ Surfer (best for content optimization) ‍ Gumloop (best for SEO automation workflows) ‍ Ahrefs (best for competitor & backlink research) ‍ Semrush (best for all-in-one SEO management) ‍ KeySearch (best for budget keyword research) ‍ SE Ranking (best for affordable rank tracking + audits) ‍ Google Keyword Planner (best for search volume & CPC estimates) ‍ Bing Webmaster Tools (best for free technical audits) ‍ AlsoAsked (best for H2 heading ideas) ‍ AnswerThePublic (best for finding long-tail queries) ‍ SimilarWeb (best for analyzing competitor traffic) ‍ ProductRank.ai (best for brand tracking in AI search) ‍ Google Trends (best for trend spotting + prioritization) ‍ Nightwatch (best for local rank tracking) ‍ Screaming Frog (best for technical SEO audits) ‍ Clearscope (best for content scoring & topic coverage) ‍ AirOps (best for AI-powered workflows) ‍ Claude (Anthropic) (best for content proofreading) ‍ Keywords Everywhere (best for in-SERP keyword metrics) ‍ Google Analytics 4 (best for site analytics) ‍ Looker Studio (best for custom SEO client dashboards) ‍ Webflow (best for building SEO-optimize sites) Let’s go over each one in depth. 1. Google Search Console Category: Technical SEO & Site Health Best for: First-party data + indexing Ease of use: Beginner to Intermediate Pricing: Free If there's only one SEO tool you should use it's Google Search Console. This is your source of truth for how you're showing up in Google. You'll be able to see what keywords your website rank for, what position you're ranking in, and how many organic clicks you're getting to your website. Having this set up for every website property you work on is super important. Later, I'll show you a tool to automate things like site audits, topical authority discovery, and on-page SEO, using GSC as an integration inside of an AI agent building platform GSC is an amazing tool that I check every day. Even though the data takes around 24 to 48 hours to update, it is the only resource in terms of getting first-party data from Google. There are many different ways you can use Google Search Console. Of course, you can use it for tracking your own pages and keywords, but there are also a few different use cases that I use it for, like using the compare feature to see which pages on my site are losing traffic and need to be updated. And also on the side of content updates, figuring out what keywords I'm getting a lot of impressions for but not a lot of clicks and adding that into my pages. I have some guides on my site for this that you can check out here . This is where you'll also submit your sitemap and request indexing of new pages or pages that you just updated. Who is Google Search Console for? Google Search Console is completely free to use, and it's designed for every single person that is trying to grow a website through SEO, whether you're a beginner, intermediate, or advanced. Pros and cons Here are some of the pros and cons with Google Search Console: Pros: It's the main source of truth for first-party data as it relates to SEO rankings on Google. Gives you clear visibility into what's happening with your website. It's completely free to use. Cons: It takes a while for the data to actually show, but this, to be honest, is not a big deal. It's only for information related to your website, so you can't use it for analyzing competitors. Google Search Console rating and reviews Here are what people rate Google Search Console on third-party review sites: G2: 4.7 out of 5 star rating (from +419 reviews ) Capterra: 4.8 out of 5 star rating (from +207 reviews ) 2. Google Autocomplete Category: Keyword & Topic Research Best for: Search-intent discovery Ease of use: Beginner Pricing: Free This is my favorite way to figure out what keywords to target, and it's using Google Autocomplete, or sometimes referred to as Google Auto-suggest. This is when you open up a window in incognito mode and go to simply google.com and start typing in a seed keyword and see what Google auto-completes. This will then give you long-tail keyword ideas to go after that people are searching for in real time. This is actually the tool that I've used to find hidden gem keywords that have turned into some of my highest traffic blog posts to date. Even right now, some of the highest-visited blogs on this site that have been read well over 100,000 times (I have multiple of them) have been found through using Google Autocomplete. Who is Google Autocomplete for? But to take it a step further, I actually combine this tool with the one we just talked about, Google Keyword Planner, and it's how I find hidden gem keywords. Some people also refer to these as "zero volume" keywords. I actually made a YouTube video on this that you can watch here: There are no real pros or cons to review for this tool, and it's completely free to use. It's pretty much just using Google, so I'm not going to include pros/cons or ratings information here. 3. Surfer Category: Content optimization Best for: Writing SEO-focused blogs Ease of use: Beginner to intermediate Pricing: Starts at $99 per month Founded in 2017, Surfer SEO is an SEO and content optimization tool that promises to help you boost your visibility in Google, ChatGPT, and other AI search engines. It's actually a tool that I've used for a few years now, and I find it to be a staple in any SEO or content marketer's workflow stack. How Surfer Works At its core, Surfer originally started as a content optimization tool , and this is widely what I have used it for in the past. Essentially, what you do is create reports based off certain keywords you want to go after, and Surfer helps you create a content outline based off your target keyword. What the platform does is it scrapes through all the top-ranking web pages for a given keyword, figures out what are common keywords used within those articles, and then spits them back out into your content brief inside of Surfer. So you can write an article targeting a keyword that is matching the correct intent and is giving you a bunch of optimization recommendations like what keywords to include, how long the word count should be, how many headings you should ideally have, etc. But since its optimization days, Surfer has launched new features like Surfer AI that helps you write content using AI in your own branded voice, and it also now allows you to show up and optimize for AI chatbots. They also have a bunch of free tools like an AI content detector tool and an AI content humanizer tool . Again, it's debatable on the accuracy of these tools, not just from Surfer but from pretty much any company out there. But it's nice if they include these for free, so you don't even need to be on a paid plan to get access to it. Who is Surfer for? As someone who's led content marketing, started an SEO agency, and runs a media company (the one you're reading on right now), I think Surfer can actually be used for anybody that creates editorial SEO content. Meaning their goal is to create amazing content for their own website or their company's website with the goal of having that content show up high in search engines based on specific keywords their potential customers are searching for. Pricing plans Surfer has three pricing tiers, and you also get a 20% discount if you pay annually, but I'm going to just list out the monthly prices below because that's generally what most people, like me, care about first. Here are Surfer's plans: Essential: This runs you $99 per month and gives you pretty much everything you need to generate reports and publish content that is optimized around specific keywords. It also has built-in templates so you can stay on brand and add in your own custom voice. Scale: This runs you $219 per month, and it gives you everything in Essential except you get five times higher limits. So what this means is you'll get more keyword reports that you can generate, you'll get more content monitoring reports, and you'll even get advanced topical maps to help you get a better idea of what type of content you should be creating based off of what already works on your site. Enterprise: This is totally custom pricing, and it's tailored to whatever businesses need and whatever rate limits they need. So you'll get everything in the Scale plan, but it'll also come with white labeling, API access, and SSO logins, which are pretty important for larger organizations. Pros and cons This wouldn't be a real review without a pros and cons section, as all of my reviews on this blog aim to be as unbiased as possible. However, I do tend to mention only tools that I have personally used and actually like. Here are some of the pros and cons of Surfer: Pros: The content optimization reports are amazing. If you're looking to better optimize your existing content for SEO, it's an amazing feature. It can easily integrate with Google Docs or WordPress. I love the Google Docs integration because I write everything in a Google Doc—even this blog post that you're reading right now is being written in a Google Doc. If you're a larger company that cares about your brand voice and collaboration, even on the basic Essential plan you get both of those things. It's a pretty big company and a trusted tool used by Intuit, Square, ClickUp, FedEx, FreshBooks, and a ton more big companies. So I know nothing's going to break, and it has a team behind it that actually cares. Cons: While Surfer is great and I use it, I do think that people should be careful using these kinds of tools without knowing any SEO fundamentals. Here are some of the cons with using Surfer: If you're a small startup, the entry-level $100-a-month plan might be a little bit too much, and there are alternatives in the space (albeit not as great) that are about half the price. You need to have some sort of basic understanding of SEO to get the most out of the tool. If you're an absolute beginner, this is probably not a tool that's going to increase your skills by a magnitude of 10. What it really does is help you go from having an 80% page to publish to a 100% page to publish. But if you don't know how to get to that 80% on your own, then Surfer or really any other tool won't help you. No technical SEO tools built in, the platform just focuses on creating and analyzing content. Surfer rating and reviews Now let's check out some reviews of Surfer from third-party websites: G2: 4.8 out of 5 stars (from +537 user reviews ) Capterra: 4.9 out of 5 stars (from +417 user reviews ) As you can see, Surfer is a solid tool with amazing reviews from others. I recommend checking it out if you're looking for something like this. They have a 7-day money-back guarantee too, so there's no huge risk in trying it out. 4. Gumloop Category: Automation & workflows Best for: Creating SEO-automated workflows Ease of use: Intermediate Pricing: Free plan, paid plans start at $97 per month Founded in 2023, Gumloop has quickly become my favorite AI marketing tool for creating any sort of workflow, including SEO workflows. How Gumloop works Gumloop is an AI agent builder that helps you build any sort of AI workflow. You can think of it as Zapier combined with ChatGPT. What this really means is that you can connect it to any of the tools that you use in your SEO tech stack and combine it with any LLM (like ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, etc.) to give your tools and workflows an AI layer. It essentially helps you become an AI engineer without needing to know how to code. The great thing about Gumloop is that many of the tools that are built in, like access to ChatGPT or even Semrush, are free to use, so you don't even have to pay for an extra account on those other platforms. For example, you can create an AI agent that scrapes competitors and monitors them through Semrush's data, and then you can feed that information to a Google Doc or a Slack message that automatically sends you reports. Or you can take that information and give it to the ChatGPT node in Gumloop and prompt it to create a blog outline, which can then send that to a Google Doc for you to write. And there's just so much more. It pretty much becomes like an AI SEO assistant in your workflow of doing SEO at your job, whether that's working in-house or working at an agency or being even a freelancer. It's like a junior-level SEO employee. But as with all AI tools, their effectiveness depends on how well you can train them. So I mentioned it's more of an intermediate/advanced tool because you have to be a pretty decent SEO already so that you can train it and create an AI SEO agent that actually helps you double, sometimes even triple your productivity. Who is Gumloop for? Gumloop is great SEO professionals and content marketers who want to automate repetitive tasks in their SEO workflows. It's actually really powerful if you're a freelancer or agency owner that manages multiple clients, or you work in an in-house team handling a big website with lots of SEO operations. The tool really shines in what I know a lot of big companies use it for, which is for competitor analysis and for creating automated reports. However, it's more than just an SEO tool, you can literally use it for any part in your marketing workflow. I discovered this tool about 7 months ago, and I loved it so much that I flew out to San Francisco and met the Gumloop team. Here's a picture of me in their office in front of their logo (lol): Me at the Gumloop office And their CEO Max was generous enough to give me a 20% off discount for any of my readers that want to use the paid plan. Again, if you want 20% off any paid plan, use code MARKETERMILK at checkout. Pros and cons of Gumloop But this wouldn't be a real review without looking at the pros and cons, so let's look at those. Integrate your Google Analytics data and even use Semrush for free inside of Gumloop to build out genetic workflows that are leveraging real data, whether from your own website or your competitors. I've met the UI/UX designers on the team at Gumloop, and they're absolute legends, so I'm not surprised at how nice the tool looks and how intuitive it is. There's a feature called Gummie, which is essentially the chatbot in the tool, and when you're creating your workflows, you can use Gummie to help you either fix any areas within an existing workflow that you've created yourself manually, or Gummie can help you even go out and build that entire workflow from scratch. Gumloop rating and reviews Because Gumloop is so new, and they are focused more on building out their product (over marketing), there aren’t a lot of reviews. But, I did write an in-depth Gumloop review if you want to check it out. As you can see, this is still a very underrated tool, but it's growing really fast and it's actually used by teams at Webflow, Instacart, Shopify, and a ton of other big brands internally, so that should show just how powerful the tool is. 5. Ahrefs Category: Competitor & backlink research Best for: Analyzing competitor sites and backlink profiles Ease of use: Beginner to expert Pricing: Starts at $108 per month If you know what SEO is, you probably already know about Ahrefs. That’s really all it comes down to on whether online SEO tools are worth the investment. For as long as people are searching (and starting their buyers’ journeys) on Google, and it’s still a primary source of traffic and leads for your business, an SEO tool will be a valuable addition to your tech stack. This is still important in 2026. 2026 update: I have used it a lot during last 12 months, and haven’t spotted any change. Their official changelog reveals a change to Lighthouse 13.0. It does however still generate ideas in a nice way and they did a great job improving the visuals. 11. My personal test of Claude Sonnet ✍️ 🔍 Price: Free. This is the leading AI content writing tool. But honestly this varies month by month as the models have ups and downs and as they keep improving in a very competitive race. For me the basic recommendation is about this: Little features that make it look like Claude was designed for writing content. Sometimes it even suggests and writes entire new articles at very high quality for you related to what you wanted, just because it saw a great related topic. Great formatting and download options also often appear. Truly magical at times. 2026 update: I still love Sonnet, and their releases during the last 12 months have only made that stronger. 12. My personal test of SEO.ai 🏆✍️ 🔍 Price: $149 per month A Danish-developed tool. I know parts of the team behind it and think they stand for good software. They have a $1 trial so you can see if it’s great. I tested it in the beginning, and have since seen demos of it adding many new features like deep web research about your topic and website publish integration. 2026 update After having a $69/month price tag for the first many years they are now charging $149/month. This is a bit steep in my opinion for what you get here, but at the same time there are many quality of life features to be had that might just suit you and make the price worth it. They offer integration to many CMS, so if you for example use a less common CMS like Drupal or Framer they also got you covered. There are a ton of competitors in this space though, for example also Surfer SEO ($219/month) and Morningscore ($69/month) on this list, so do test several and see what fits you 😊 13. My personal test of AI Optimization Checker 🤖 ✍️ Price: Free This 100% free tool is developed by the Matti Ljungberg as a hobby project as I understand it. And he just told me his monthly data/server bill is getting quite high, so let’s hope it stays free 😅 The tool lets you insert any URL and get info about how ready it is to “rank” in AI. But of course you must take it with a grain of salt, in the end much of this advice is a guide, not a rule. 14. My personal test of Screaming Frog 🤖 Price: $279 per year. Limited free version too. I experienced a big design update, which is nice. So my comments above about a design that wasn’t to my taste is now pending. To be fair, I did not spend enough time in the new version 2 to give my full verdict. One thing I do see though, is that the tool stays very classic SEO, which is by no means a bad thing, but you don’t get solid GEO features here. 16. My personal test of SE Ranking 🏆 🤖 🔍 🔗 💬 Price: $65 SE Ranking provides a complete toolbox of SEO tools. All-in-one tool. I was a customer for 2 years. However, personally, I found only their rank tracker really good. Their link tools were confusing and the data was not super. Technical SEO audit was so-so. It may have changed since I was a customer. Price/quality is sharp. Nice surprise: Their keyword data has gotten quite good in the last 1-2 years and their keyword research tool is now great. 2026 update: Nice to see the price remained stable. They did however, like many other SEO tools in the last 12 months, make a lot of adjustments to their add-ons. Meaning now a lot of features are a paid add-on. It’s quite confusing. So in that case I guess there is a hidden price increase. They added AI features which work quite well. I especially like their AI Overviews rank tracking, which is now out of beta. The tool still feels quite bulky and slow and the UX is not my cup of tea. But I would still say SE Ranking is one of the tools that keep improving and growing year after year. 17. My personal test of AccuRanker 🏆 🔍 Price: $224 per month AccuRanker is a Danish-developed rank-tracking tool. That is, they focus on tracking keywords and their ranking on Google. They are really good at this and help big companies and agencies to track thousands of keywords. I was a customer for 1 year. So if you have a big rank tracking need and want to be able to filter deep into that data, AccuRanker is worth checking out. Several new clients of ours have mentioned Morningscore as a good alternative to Accuranker . Of course, this depends on the need. Accuranker are kings when it comes to large and complex keyword tracking needs. And their filtering and tagging of keywords is quite deep. 2026 update: Here I am reviewing Accuranker. But they also released a new tool called AccuLLM recently, starting at $199/month. I guess AccuLLM could be seen as an add-on which allows you to track AI prompts, like several other tools on this list also allows. Also, their relatively new search volume engine has gotten quite good now. They combine data sources to give you a more precise search volume on keywords. 18. Loved by marketers at "My favorite marketing newsletter I’m subscribed to.” — Faith Storey, Freelance Marketer Feed Services SaaS SEO agency Content marketing course Topics Blog About Join free ← All posts 24 best SEO tools I'm using in 2026 (free + paid) Over the past decade, I have collected the best SEO tools (free and paid) that I use almost daily. Today, I reveal them all to you in this mega guide. Post by Omid G | June 14, 2026 I've been doing SEO for a decade. Most notably, I led SEO at Webflow (a $4.2B company) and then built my blog to +150K visitors/month from SEO all by myself. I've also worked with dozens of software companies to help them with their SEO revenue growth. It's safe to say that I've tested and used all of the best SEO tools on the market. And I'm constantly looking for the newest tools that can give me and my clients an edge. In this post, I'm breaking down 24 of the best SEO software and tools (across different categories) so you can pick what's best for your specific needs. I'll also include an "ease of use" score for each tool (beginner, intermediate, or advanced) to help you choose tools that match your skill level. These aren't in a particular order, but they lean a bit more on the side of how much I value them. Also, I tried to group many of the tools for logical clarity so you can easily find what you're looking for. Don't worry, this is not a biased post by some SEO company trying to sell you their tool. This post is 100% written by me. I only recommend the SEO tools I've used, and will talk about what I like and don't like about each of them. No AI-generated slop, just real insights from someone who uses these tools every single day. What is an SEO tool? An SEO (search engine optimization) tool is a platform that helps you plan and strategize ways to improve your site's visibility in search engines. This is not just limited to Google. This includes Bing, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and all the other search engines on the market. These tools all do different things. Some of them help you with keyword research , some of them help are search ranking tools that help you analyze competitors' traffic and backlinks, some of them help you create content that is optimized for search engines, some of them help you create automated SEO workflows, and some of them help you improve the technical health of your website. Some of the tools we'll go over in this post aim to do all the things I just mentioned, while some of them only do one specific thing very well. Overall, I've used every single tool on this list and have written a comprehensive review of all of them below. But my goal is to help you understand what tool to use for yourself, so let's first go over what I consider to be the best SEO tools to use. What do I consider the best SEO tools? For beginners, I generally recommend using the free SEO tools that Google gives you. This includes using Google Autocomplete, Google Keyword Planner, Google Search Console, and even Google Trends. With just these free tools alone, I've been able to rank #1 really fast. In fact, here are my top SEO tools if you prefer to watch how I use them: The Google tools are some of the best free tools (and I'll show you more in this post) that I think you should start out with first. From there, you want to get into the content creation part, and some of the tools that I believe are the best there would be Surfer, Claude, or Clearscope. When it comes to keyword research and analyzing competitors, my favorite tools are Ahrefs, Semrush, and using Google Autocomplete. And when it comes to creating SEO automations, my favorite tool by far is Gumloop. Again, all of these we're going to go over below. Okay, no more rambling. Let's get into my picks for the best SEO software. 24 best SEO tools I've personally tested in 2026 Here are the best SEO tools right now: ‍ Google Search Console (best for first-party data + indexing) ‍ Google Autocomplete (best for search-intent discovery) ‍ Surfer (best for content optimization) ‍ Gumloop (best for SEO automation workflows) ‍ Ahrefs (best for competitor & backlink research) ‍ Semrush (best for all-in-one SEO management) ‍ KeySearch (best for budget keyword research) ‍ SE Ranking (best for affordable rank tracking + audits) ‍ Google Keyword Planner (best for search volume & CPC estimates) ‍ Bing Webmaster Tools (best for free technical audits) ‍ AlsoAsked (best for H2 heading ideas) ‍ AnswerThePublic (best for finding long-tail queries) ‍ SimilarWeb (best for analyzing competitor traffic) ‍ ProductRank.ai (best for brand tracking in AI search) ‍ Google Trends (best for trend spotting + prioritization) ‍ Nightwatch (best for local rank tracking) ‍ Screaming Frog (best for technical SEO audits) ‍ Clearscope (best for content scoring & topic coverage) ‍ AirOps (best for AI-powered workflows) ‍ Claude (Anthropic) (best for content proofreading) ‍ Keywords Everywhere (best for in-SERP keyword metrics) ‍ Google Analytics 4 (best for site analytics) ‍ Looker Studio (best for custom SEO client dashboards) ‍ Webflow (best for building SEO-optimize sites) Let’s go over each one in depth. 1. Google Search Console Category: Technical SEO & Site Health Best for: First-party data + indexing Ease of use: Beginner to Intermediate Pricing: Free If there's only one SEO tool you should use it's Google Search Console. This is your source of truth for how you're showing up in Google. You'll be able to see what keywords your website rank for, what position you're ranking in, and how many organic clicks you're getting to your website. Having this set up for every website property you work on is super important. Later, I'll show you a tool to automate things like site audits, topical authority discovery, and on-page SEO, using GSC as an integration inside of an AI agent building platform GSC is an amazing tool that I check every day. Even though the data takes around 24 to 48 hours to update, it is the only resource in terms of getting first-party data from Google. There are many different ways you can use Google Search Console. Of course, you can use it for tracking your own pages and keywords, but there are also a few different use cases that I use it for, like using the compare feature to see which pages on my site are losing traffic and need to be updated. And also on the side of content updates, figuring out what keywords I'm getting a lot of impressions for but not a lot of clicks and adding that into my pages. I have some guides on my site for this that you can check out here . This is where you'll also submit your sitemap and request indexing of new pages or pages that you just updated. Who is Google Search Console for? Google Search Console is completely free to use, and it's designed for every single person that is trying to grow a website through SEO, whether you're a beginner, intermediate, or advanced. Pros and cons Here are some of the pros and cons with Google Search Console: Pros: It's the main source of truth for first-party data as it relates to SEO rankings on Google. Gives you clear visibility into what's happening with your website. It's completely free to use. Cons: It takes a while for the data to actually show, but this, to be honest, is not a big deal. It's only for information related to your website, so you can't use it for analyzing competitors. Google Search Console rating and reviews Here are what people rate Google Search Console on third-party review sites: G2: 4.7 out of 5 star rating (from +419 reviews ) Capterra: 4.8 out of 5 star rating (from +207 reviews ) 2. Google Autocomplete Category: Keyword & Topic Research Best for: Search-intent discovery Ease of use: Beginner Pricing: Free This is my favorite way to figure out what keywords to target, and it's using Google Autocomplete, or sometimes referred to as Google Auto-suggest. This is when you open up a window in incognito mode and go to simply google.com and start typing in a seed keyword and see what Google auto-completes. This will then give you long-tail keyword ideas to go after that people are searching for in real time. This is actually the tool that I've used to find hidden gem keywords that have turned into some of my highest traffic blog posts to date. Even right now, some of the highest-visited blogs on this site that have been read well over 100,000 times (I have multiple of them) have been found through using Google Autocomplete. Who is Google Autocomplete for? But to take it a step further, I actually combine this tool with the one we just talked about, Google Keyword Planner, and it's how I find hidden gem keywords. Some people also refer to these as "zero volume" keywords. I actually made a YouTube video on this that you can watch here: There are no real pros or cons to review for this tool, and it's completely free to use. It's pretty much just using Google, so I'm not going to include pros/cons or ratings information here. 3. Surfer Category: Content optimization Best for: Writing SEO-focused blogs Ease of use: Beginner to intermediate Pricing: Starts at $99 per month Founded in 2017, Surfer SEO is an SEO and content optimization tool that promises to help you boost your visibility in Google, ChatGPT, and other AI search engines. It's actually a tool that I've used for a few years now, and I find it to be a staple in any SEO or content marketer's workflow stack. How Surfer Works At its core, Surfer originally started as a content optimization tool , and this is widely what I have used it for in the past. Essentially, what you do is create reports based off certain keywords you want to go after, and Surfer helps you create a content outline based off your target keyword. What the platform does is it scrapes through all the top-ranking web pages for a given keyword, figures out what are common keywords used within those articles, and then spits them back out into your content brief inside of Surfer. So you can write an article targeting a keyword that is matching the correct intent and is giving you a bunch of optimization recommendations like what keywords to include, how long the word count should be, how many headings you should ideally have, etc. But since its optimization days, Surfer has launched new features like Surfer AI that helps you write content using AI in your own branded voice, and it also now allows you to show up and optimize for AI chatbots. They also have a bunch of free tools like an AI content detector tool and an AI content humanizer tool . Again, it's debatable on the accuracy of these tools, not just from Surfer but from pretty much any company out there. But it's nice if they include these for free, so you don't even need to be on a paid plan to get access to it. Who is Surfer for? As someone who's led content marketing, started an SEO agency, and runs a media company (the one you're reading on right now), I think Surfer can actually be used for anybody that creates editorial SEO content. Meaning their goal is to create amazing content for their own website or their company's website with the goal of having that content show up high in search engines based on specific keywords their potential customers are searching for. Pricing plans Surfer has three pricing tiers, and you also get a 20% discount if you pay annually, but I'm going to just list out the monthly prices below because that's generally what most people, like me, care about first. Here are Surfer's plans: Essential: This runs you $99 per month and gives you pretty much everything you need to generate reports and publish content that is optimized around specific keywords. It also has built-in templates so you can stay on brand and add in your own custom voice. Scale: This runs you $219 per month, and it gives you everything in Essential except you get five times higher limits. So what this means is you'll get more keyword reports that you can generate, you'll get more content monitoring reports, and you'll even get advanced topical maps to help you get a better idea of what type of content you should be creating based off of what already works on your site. Enterprise: This is totally custom pricing, and it's tailored to whatever businesses need and whatever rate limits they need. So you'll get everything in the Scale plan, but it'll also come with white labeling, API access, and SSO logins, which are pretty important for larger organizations. Pros and cons This wouldn't be a real review without a pros and cons section, as all of my reviews on this blog aim to be as unbiased as possible. However, I do tend to mention only tools that I have personally used and actually like. Here are some of the pros and cons of Surfer: Pros: The content optimization reports are amazing. If you're looking to better optimize your existing content for SEO, it's an amazing feature. It can easily integrate with Google Docs or WordPress. I love the Google Docs integration because I write everything in a Google Doc—even this blog post that you're reading right now is being written in a Google Doc. If you're a larger company that cares about your brand voice and collaboration, even on the basic Essential plan you get both of those things. It's a pretty big company and a trusted tool used by Intuit, Square, ClickUp, FedEx, FreshBooks, and a ton more big companies. So I know nothing's going to break, and it has a team behind it that actually cares. Cons: While Surfer is great and I use it, I do think that people should be careful using these kinds of tools without knowing any SEO fundamentals. Here are some of the cons with using Surfer: If you're a small startup, the entry-level $100-a-month plan might be a little bit too much, and there are alternatives in the space (albeit not as great) that are about half the price. You need to have some sort of basic understanding of SEO to get the most out of the tool. If you're an absolute beginner, this is probably not a tool that's going to increase your skills by a magnitude of 10. What it really does is help you go from having an 80% page to publish to a 100% page to publish. But if you don't know how to get to that 80% on your own, then Surfer or really any other tool won't help you. No technical SEO tools built in, the platform just focuses on creating and analyzing content. Surfer rating and reviews Now let's check out some reviews of Surfer from third-party websites: G2: 4.8 out of 5 stars (from +537 user reviews ) Capterra: 4.9 out of 5 stars (from +417 user reviews ) As you can see, Surfer is a solid tool with amazing reviews from others. I recommend checking it out if you're looking for something like this. They have a 7-day money-back guarantee too, so there's no huge risk in trying it out. 4. Gumloop Category: Automation & workflows Best for: Creating SEO-automated workflows Ease of use: Intermediate Pricing: Free plan, paid plans start at $97 per month Founded in 2023, Gumloop has quickly become my favorite AI marketing tool for creating any sort of workflow, including SEO workflows. How Gumloop works Gumloop is an AI agent builder that helps you build any sort of AI workflow. You can think of it as Zapier combined with ChatGPT. What this really means is that you can connect it to any of the tools that you use in your SEO tech stack and combine it with any LLM (like ChatGPT, Claude, Grok, etc.) to give your tools and workflows an AI layer. It essentially helps you become an AI engineer without needing to know how to code. The great thing about Gumloop is that many of the tools that are built in, like access to ChatGPT or even Semrush, are free to use, so you don't even have to pay for an extra account on those other platforms. For example, you can create an AI agent that scrapes competitors and monitors them through Semrush's data, and then you can feed that information to a Google Doc or a Slack message that automatically sends you reports. Or you can take that information and give it to the ChatGPT node in Gumloop and prompt it to create a blog outline, which can then send that to a Google Doc for you to write. And there's just so much more. It pretty much becomes like an AI SEO assistant in your workflow of doing SEO at your job, whether that's working in-house or working at an agency or being even a freelancer. It's like a junior-level SEO employee. But as with all AI tools, their effectiveness depends on how well you can train them. So I mentioned it's more of an intermediate/advanced tool because you have to be a pretty decent SEO already so that you can train it and create an AI SEO agent that actually helps you double, sometimes even triple your productivity. Who is Gumloop for? Gumloop is great SEO professionals and content marketers who want to automate repetitive tasks in their SEO workflows. It's actually really powerful if you're a freelancer or agency owner that manages multiple clients, or you work in an in-house team handling a big website with lots of SEO operations. The tool really shines in what I know a lot of big companies use it for, which is for competitor analysis and for creating automated reports. However, it's more than just an SEO tool, you can literally use it for any part in your marketing workflow. I discovered this tool about 7 months ago, and I loved it so much that I flew out to San Francisco and met the Gumloop team. Here's a picture of me in their office in front of their logo (lol): Me at the Gumloop office And their CEO Max was generous enough to give me a 20% off discount for any of my readers that want to use the paid plan. You can use code MARKETERMILK at checkout for 20% off (and no, they're not paying me to say that or include them in this list, I just love them). Pricing plans Here are Gumloop's paid plans: Free: $0 a month, and this comes with 5,000 credits, which is more than enough to build out your first flow and really see the power of the tool. Pro: $37 per month and starts at 20,000 credits per month. Enterprise: Custom. This is completely custom pricing based off of what you need. Again, if you want 20% off any paid plan, use code MARKETERMILK at checkout. Pros and cons of Gumloop But this wouldn't be a real review without looking at the pros and cons, so let's look at those. Pros: Build any SEO workflow and automate it with AI agents. Integrate your Google Analytics data and even use Semrush for free inside of Gumloop to build out genetic workflows that are leveraging real data, whether from your own website or your competitors. The free plan is super generous, and you can create your first AI agent with it, probably for free. It has the best UI and UX of any AI SaaS tool I've seen. I've met the UI/UX designers on the team at Gumloop, and they're absolute legends, so I'm not surprised at how nice the tool looks and how intuitive it is. There's a feature called Gummie, which is essentially the chatbot in the tool, and when you're creating your workflows, you can use Gummie to help you either fix any areas within an existing workflow that you've created yourself manually, or Gummie can help you even go out and build that entire workflow from scratch. Cons: No smaller tiered plan to test out beyond the free plan. The entry level plan might be tough for indie creators on a budget. Somethings can break at times because the team is constantly shipping new features. They are fast to respond though if you reach out. Gumloop rating and reviews Because Gumloop is so new, and they are focused more on building out their product (over marketing), there aren’t a lot of reviews. But, I did write an in-depth Gumloop review if you want to check it out. As you can see, this is still a very underrated tool, but it's growing really fast and it's actually used by teams at Webflow, Instacart, Shopify, and a ton of other big brands internally, so that should show just how powerful the tool is. 5. Ahrefs Category: Competitor & backlink research Best for: Analyzing competitor sites and backlink profiles Ease of use: Beginner to expert Pricing: Starts at $108 per month If you know what SEO is, you probably already know about Ahrefs. Ahrefs is an SEO-first tool, although they are migrating over into being an overall marketing platform for all search engines and LLMs. How Ahrefs works Personally, I use Ahrefs almost every single day to track how my website is performing, how my client sites are performing, and how other websites in my clients' niches are performing. There are really different ways you can use Ahrefs. I find that it's great for doing pretty much anything with SEO. In fact, if there's probably only one tool you will ever pay for that is genuinely useful besides something like Surfer, it's going to be Ahrefs. But I find it's especially good as a backlink checker if you are trying to analyze competitors and their link building strategies through their Site Explorer feature, or even use it as a keyword explorer and broader keyword research tool to help you identify specific topics you might be thinking about, although there are some free tools that I think I like even more than Ahrefs for keyword research that I'll cover in this list below. Who is Ahrefs for? Ahrefs is great for any level from beginner to intermediate to expert, and it's great if you work at a startup and you run SEO, it's great if you run your own company and your own websites, it's great if you're a freelancer. It fits every sort of persona that is involved in SEO or content marketing. Pricing plans Ahrefs is known to not be the cheapest tool out there, so let's look at some of the pricing plans: Lite: This starts at $108 per month and gives you up to 5 projects, 750 tracked keywords, and 500 credits per user (one credit is used per action with Ahrefs). Standard: This starts at $208 a month, gives you up to 20 projects, 2,000 tracked keywords, and unlimited credits per user. Advanced: This starts at $374 per month and gives you up to 50 projects, 10,000 tracked keywords, and a few extra features. I define an SEO tool as any software you can use to improve some aspect of a search engine optimization campaign. These tools can serve many different functions, including search query analytics, reporting automation, AI-driven content optimization recommendations, and website performance analysis. More recently, they've picked up a new job: telling you whether your brand shows up in AI-generated answers. Grow your business with marketing automation Learn how This gets tricky when you consider how many types of software marketers use for specific aspects of SEO . To try to keep some semblance of a level playing field, I excluded products that are narrowly focused on just one or two niche SEO use cases, like Moz's handy title tag tool . Instead, I focused on products that could fit into one of four distinct SEO product categories. SEO audit tools : These tools are designed primarily to perform analysis of one or more metrics related to search engine optimization efforts. Keyword research tools : The primary purpose of these tools is reporting on the search metrics of keywords or helping identify keywords to target. These don't necessarily measure ranking performance for specific webpages or domains. Rank trackers : Nearly all SEO rank trackers can perform general keyword research, but their main function is monitoring how well specific webpages or domains rank for individual keywords. They also tend to include suites of other tools for SEO-related tasks, though not as many as all-in-one tools. All-in-one tools: Similar to rank trackers, all-in-one SEO tools have many features, but their range of tools is more comprehensive. They can make tools from the other categories redundant and tend to include advanced features like automation and AI. You'll find many of the tools on my list fall into this category; that's just the way the SEO tool market is headed. I was able to dig into a lot of these tools myself (and others of them I use every day), but I wasn't able to personally test each of the dozens of options I considered. When I couldn't, I looked to firsthand accounts from real users, software demos, aggregated reviews, and Reddit forums to fill in the blanks. What makes the best SEO tool? How we evaluate and test apps Our best apps roundups are written by humans who've spent much of their careers using, testing, and writing about software. Unless explicitly stated, we spend dozens of hours researching and testing apps, using each app as it's intended to be used and evaluating it against the criteria we set for the category. We're never paid for placement in our articles from any app or for links to any site—we value the trust readers put in us to offer authentic evaluations of the categories and apps we review. For more details on our process, read the full rundown of how we select apps to feature on the Zapier blog . Since SEO tools can fall into distinct categories, nailing down what makes them great is a little complicated. To score them as objectively as possible, I reviewed dozens of products and whittled down a list of quality criteria that could apply to any category. SEO-centric functionality: Each tool has to have functionality that relates to some element of search engine optimization. They should fit into one of the categories above by specializing in a function like keyword analysis, on-page performance troubleshooting, website performance reporting, content ideation, or competitor analysis . Value: How well does the price represent the quality of the product? Tools with specific use cases should be effective enough to justify subscriptions for users with more comprehensive tools, just as comprehensive tools should have extensive feature suites, and paid tools in general should be more useful than free options. User experience: How easy is the tool to integrate, learn, and use? The learning curve should be low enough for users to reliably access any feature they need in complex tools without resorting to more familiar, less functional tools. Integrations: Since digital marketers tend to use many different software products, integration is key for SEO tools. Users should be able to integrate these tools readily into common platforms for related tasks like meetings, scheduling, reporting, and customer relationship management . Some also expose their data to an AI assistant through an MCP server, which matters if that's where your team already works. AI search visibility: Ranking in Google is only part of the job when a chunk of your audience is getting its answers from an AI assistant instead. A tool should be able to show you whether your pages are being cited in AI-generated answers, which engines it checks, and which competitors are getting mentioned when you aren't. how to get found by chatgpt and google a.text: How to Get Found in ChatGPT and AI Search in 2026 | Dynadot Domains Aftermarket Tools Resources Support EN - USD ($) Login Online Presence & SEO AI SEO in 2026: Get Found in ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, and Copilot Written by Aleksandra Vukovic Sep 01, 2026 Blog > Online Presence & SEO > Table of Contents Table of Contents Summary Getting found in AI search is not one ranking. A site can be retrieved, a brand mentioned, a page cited, and a user clicked through: four different outcomes. Traditional SEO still matters. Google says its generative AI features are rooted in core Search ranking and quality systems, while OpenAI and Microsoft still depend on accessible web content. Prioritize crawlability and indexability, clear and quotable content, consistent brand/entity information, credible third-party evidence, and separate measurement of citations and traffic. Do not make llms.txt, exotic schema, manufactured forum mentions, or hundreds of thin prompt-targeted pages your first move. What “Getting Found in AI” Actually Means Getting found in AI search is different from ranking on Google. There is no universal “#1 position in ChatGPT.” Instead, AI visibility depends on whether AI systems can find, mention, cite, and send users to your website. For a business, this can happen in four steps: Retrieved: AI can find information from your site. Mentioned: Your company, product, or brand appears in an answer. Cited: The answer links to your page. Clicked: The user follows the link to your website. A chatbot might mention your brand without linking to it, or link to a review instead of your own site. So, AI SEO is best viewed as a funnel: OpenAI’s current publisher guidance for ChatGPT Search focuses on whether a public site is accessible to OAI-SearchBot rather than promising placement for a query. The practical goal is not to “train ChatGPT on your company.” It is to make your site accessible, make key information clear and useful, establish a consistent identity, and give search and AI systems credible material to retrieve. ChatGPT vs. Google AI Mode vs. Copilot: What Changes? The fundamentals overlap, but the discovery and measurement systems differ. This table shows the fundamental adjustments that have to be made if you want to get found on ChatGPT, Google AI Mode or Microsoft Copilot. Platform How web discovery works What site owners should prioritize ChatGPT Search OpenAI uses OAI-SearchBot for search discovery and can retrieve web pages for current answers. Allow OAI-SearchBot, avoid infrastructure blocks, publish citable content, and track referrals. Google AI Mode / AI Overviews Content comes from Google’s Search index and ranking systems; query fan-out can search related subtopics. Normal Google indexability, useful original content, technical SEO, and Search Console. Microsoft Copilot Web-grounded Copilot experiences use Bing search infrastructure. Bing indexability, Bing Webmaster Tools, crawl health, and strong source content. ChatGPT Search OpenAI’s web crawler documentation separates OAI-SearchBot from GPTBot . OAI-SearchBot supports search discovery, while GPTBot is associated with content that may be used to improve generative AI models. A publisher can therefore allow search discovery while choosing a different policy for GPTBot. OpenAI’s publisher FAQ says pages should not block OAI-SearchBot if the goal is inclusion in ChatGPT summaries and snippets. Google AI Mode and AI Overviews Google’s guide to optimizing for generative AI features says traditional SEO remains relevant because AI Overviews and AI Mode rely on core Search ranking and quality systems and retrieve information from the Search index. There is no separate AI-only submission process or special schema required just to appear. Google also describes query fan-out , where its systems can run multiple related searches for different parts of a complex question. That rewards useful topical coverage, not dozens of near-duplicate pages for prompt variations. Microsoft Copilot Microsoft documents that web-grounded Copilot experiences can send generated queries to the Bing search service for grounding . Bing’s AI Performance dashboard, launched in public preview on February 10, 2026, reports citations across Microsoft Copilot, AI-generated Bing answers, and selected partner integrations. Bing’s announcement says it includes total citations, cited pages, trends, and sampled grounding queries, while warning that these metrics are not rankings or authority scores. The takeaway Optimize one strong website, but verify visibility separately across all three ecosystems. 3. Step 1: Make the Site Technically Discoverable Before rewriting content for AI, make sure the systems can reach it. Dynadot’s technical SEO audit provides a broader workflow for crawlability, indexation, canonicalization, HTTPS, performance, and sitemap issues. Check robots.txt Visit yourdomain.com/robots.txt and look for accidental site-wide blocks such as Disallow: /. If you want content eligible for ChatGPT Search, allow OAI-SearchBot on the pages you want discovered: User-agent: OAI-SearchBot Allow: / Do not assume that allowing GPTBot accomplishes the same thing; OpenAI documents the bots separately. Check the server, CDN, and firewall too Robots.txt is only one layer. OpenAI’s crawler troubleshooting guidance notes that Cloudflare, Akamai, firewalls, bot mitigation, and CAPTCHA-style challenges can still block legitimate crawler requests and return errors such as 403 Forbidden. Confirm Google and Bing indexability Use Google Search Console’s URL Inspection and indexing reports for important pages. Set up Bing Webmaster Tools and confirm that the same URLs are crawlable and indexed there. Submit an XML sitemap to both, especially for a new site. Consolidate duplicates Choose one canonical version of each important page. There is suggestive AI-specific evidence here: a May 2026 analysis of 1,028,959 cited URLs reported that pages without query strings averaged 2.1 citations , compared with 1.6 for URLs with parameters. The 24-hour observational study does not prove causation, and Dynadot’s guide to how AI systems connect domains with brands explains that limitation. The priority is simple: make the canonical page easy to crawl and hard to confuse with another URL. Step 2: Make Every Important Page Easy for AI to Extract Once a page is accessible, the next question is whether it contains something worth extracting. The safest rule is not “write for AI.” It is make the useful part unmistakable. For informational pages: Give each page a clear primary intent. Answer the main question early. Use descriptive headings and self-contained definitions. Support claims with identifiable sources. Add firsthand examples, data, or comparisons where available. Update information that becomes stale. A Search Engine Land analysis spanning 15 domains , almost 2 million monthly organic sessions , and roughly 7,500 ChatGPT referral sessions found that 72.4% of cited blog posts contained an identifiable “answer capsule,” while 52.2% contained original data or brand-owned insight. The citation analysis is observational, so these traits should not be called confirmed ranking factors. A useful pattern is: Direct answer → explanation → evidence → example → limitation or exception Google’s 2026 generative AI optimization guide also advises site owners to prioritize useful, non-commodity content rather than arbitrary “chunking” rules or AEO/GEO hacks. Step 3: Make Your Brand and Entity Clear AI visibility is not only about a page. The system also has to understand who the information belongs to . Keep these identity signals consistent: Primary brand and company name. Primary domain and canonical URLs. About-page details. Author names and bios. Contact and location information where relevant. Google Business Profile and legitimate industry profiles. Structured data such as Organization or LocalBusiness can make explicit facts easier for search engines to understand, but it is not an AI-ranking switch. Google says there is no special schema markup required for generative AI search . Your domain provides a consistent public home for the brand. Dynadot’s guide to how AI systems connect domains with brands examines the evidence and its limits. Do not turn that into a claim that a particular extension makes ChatGPT trust you. In the dataset discussed in our guide, .COM, .ORG, .IO, and .AI pages each averaged 1.7 citations per cited URL during the study window. That observational result argues against treating a TLD as an automatic AI citation advantage. Choose a domain because it is memorable, credible to your audience, defensible as a brand, and easy to use consistently. Step 4: Build Evidence Outside Your Own Website Your site can say your company is excellent. Independent sources make claims easier to verify. Useful external evidence can include editorial backlinks, independent coverage, genuine reviews, industry listings, expert citations, partner pages, original research referenced elsewhere, and real community discussions. Learn how to earn relevant referring domains and why unique referring sites are different from raw backlink count. Practitioners are also warning against treating GEO as a shortcut. In a March 2026 interview, SEO consultant Lily Ray discussed why scaled, self-promotional content and short-lived GEO tactics can backfire, while recognizable expertise and authority are more durable. The interview on AI Search and GEO spam is practitioner commentary, not proof of ranking factors. What about planting brand mentions on Reddit? Marketers have experimented with brand-favorable forum posts in hopes that AI systems will retrieve them. But, covert promotion can violate community rules, be removed, damage credibility, and disappear as citation-source preferences change. Verdict Participate when you can add genuine expertise; do not build a strategy around fabricated conversations or sock-puppet mentions. What about `llms.txt`? Google’s 2026 AI optimization guidance specifically says site owners can ignore unnecessary AI text files such as llms.txt for Google Search. Verdict Optional for ecosystems that explicitly support it, not a priority Google optimization. What about mass-producing pages for AI prompts? Google warns against scaled content created mainly to manipulate search systems and advises against unnecessary query-variation pages built around AEO/GEO tricks. Verdict Cover real customer questions deeply; do not create hundreds of thin “ChatGPT-targeted” variants. Step 5: Measure AI Visibility Without Pretending It Is Google Rankings AI visibility needs its own measurement model. Start with a fixed set of approximately 10–20 representative prompts , a practical working framework for a small business, not an industry standard. Include discovery, comparison, and decision prompts, then record: Was the brand mentioned? Was your own site cited? Which third-party pages were cited? Which competitors appeared? Did AI referrals or conversions change? Run the same prompt set on a regular schedule. Do not interpret one answer as a stable ranking; generative results can change with wording, location, freshness, model updates, and retrieved sources. How to Run a Repeatable AI Visibility Test? To measure AI visibility consistently, use the same set of prompts across ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, and Microsoft Copilot instead of testing random questions each time. Create 10–20 prompts that reflect how real customers might search for your product, service, or category, then record whether your brand is mentioned, whether your website is cited, which competitors appear, and which sources the AI uses. For cleaner comparisons, keep the wording of each prompt unchanged between tests. Run them on a regular schedule, such as monthly, and record the date, platform, response, cited URLs, and any referral traffic that follows. Because generative answers can vary between sessions, focus on patterns across repeated tests rather than treating one response as a fixed ranking. Example prompt: What are the best website creator for small businesses that need domain registration, email, and website-building tools? You could then track: Whether your brand is mentioned. Whether your brand is cited directly. Which your brand’s page is cited. Which competing companies appear. Which third-party sources influence the answer. Whether the result changes when the same prompt is tested again the following month. Track ChatGPT referral traffic OpenAI says ChatGPT referral URLs include `utm_source=chatgpt.com` , allowing publishers to identify inbound traffic in analytics. OpenAI’s publisher FAQ is the first-party reference for this behavior. Track landing page, engagement, conversion, and revenue where applicable — not merely sessions. For context, Semrush reported 206% growth in outbound ChatGPT referral traffic from January 2025 to January 2026 in a 17-month clickstream analysis. Semrush’s study is a third-party market estimate, so your own analytics should remain the decision source. Use Google’s dedicated generative AI reporting where available On June 3, 2026, Google announced dedicated Search Generative AI performance reports for Search and Discover, initially rolling them out to a subset of websites. Google’s announcement lists impressions, pages, countries, devices for Search, and performance over time among the initial dimensions. Use Bing Webmaster Tools AI Performance Bing’s AI Performance dashboard reports total citations, average cited pages, page-level activity, trends, and sampled grounding queries. Microsoft explicitly says those metrics do not indicate page ranking, authority, or placement in an individual answer. Treat third-party AI visibility scores as vendor metrics. Google warns that third parties do not have access to its internal ranking or AI systems. What to Do First: The 30-Minute / 30-Day Priority Checklist If you are starting from zero, do not begin with a GEO tool subscription, a schema overhaul, or an llms.txt file. In the first 30 minutes Check important pages in Google. Confirm the homepage and key pages are indexed. Open robots.txt. Look for accidental crawl blocks and confirm your OAI-SearchBot policy. Check Bing Webmaster Tools. Confirm Bing can discover important URLs. Test five real customer prompts. Run the same questions through ChatGPT, Google AI Mode, and Copilot and record mentions and citations. Check brand identity. Make sure the domain, company description, location, and core details are consistent across major profiles. During the next 30 days Week 1: Fix eligibility. Resolve crawl blocks, canonicals, indexing problems, sitemap issues, broken redirects, or WAF rules affecting legitimate crawlers. Week 2: Improve citation-worthy pages. Add direct answers, firsthand expertise, evidence, comparisons, examples, and clear sourcing rather than simply making pages longer. Week 3: Strengthen entity and external evidence. Standardize brand information and pursue legitimate mentions, partnerships, reviews, press, and relevant links. Week 4: Measure again. Repeat the prompt set and compare mentions, citations, cited third parties, AI referrals, and conversions against the baseline. If you are still at the website-launch stage, our partnership lets you launch a website with Dynadot and Wix from a Dynadot domain into a Wix website-building flow. Once the site is live, make it crawlable, publish material customers actually need, and build a consistent identity around the domain. For deeper technical SEO, content, domain, and AI visibility guidance, continue with Dynadot’s SEO and AI visibility guides . The priority order is deliberately unglamorous: Eligibility → useful content → entity clarity → external authority → measurement. That is more defensible in 2026 than trying to reverse-engineer one temporary citation pattern, and it improves the website you would want search engines, AI systems, and customers to find anyway. FAQ How do I get my website to show up in ChatGPT? Make the site publicly accessible and do not block OAI-SearchBot on pages you want eligible for ChatGPT Search. Then focus on clear, useful content and credible web signals; OpenAI does not provide a guaranteed placement mechanism for a particular query. Is AI SEO different from traditional SEO? AI SEO adds retrieval, citation, and entity-clarity considerations, but it does not replace traditional SEO. Google says its AI Search features rely on core Search ranking and quality systems, and ChatGPT and Copilot also depend on accessible web content. Does a .AI or .COM domain make a website more likely to be cited by AI? There is no reliable evidence that choosing .AI or .COM automatically improves citation probability. One large 2026 observational dataset found the same average citation rate for .COM, .ORG, .IO, and .AI URLs during its measurement window. How should a small business measure whether AI SEO is working? Track a stable set of representative prompts, brand mentions, citations to your pages, third-party sources cited instead, AI referral traffic, and downstream conversions. Use first-party reporting such as Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools where available.
